# Phantom Secrets

Your agent can call the API. The key stays in a local vault.

Phantom replaces managed secrets in `.env` with `phm_` placeholders. A proxy on `127.0.0.1` adds the vault value only to the auth header of a matched route. Secret values are not printed, logged, or returned to a model.

## 30-second start

```bash
brew tap ashlrai/phantom && brew trust --formula ashlrai/phantom/phantom && brew install ashlrai/phantom/phantom
phantom init
phantom setup --client claude
phantom status --json
phantom list --json
phantom check --log agent-transcript.jsonl --json
```

Linux and Windows installs, and the limits of each package channel, are in [docs/distribution-status.md](docs/distribution-status.md).

`phantom status --json`, `phantom list --json`, and `phantom check --log` are value-free. The log scan reports the file, the line, and the credential shape. The same scan is MCP `phantom_check` with `log_path`.

## Ashlr ecosystem

Phantom Secrets is one of the open-source tools from Ashlr (https://ashlr.ai). Together they aim to be an autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory: agents write, test, review, and ship the code, and the human acts as a passive board member. The long-term goal is open-source recursive self-improvement (RSI), where agents improve the tools they build with. Each tool installs and runs on its own:

- Phantom (`phm`, https://phm.dev): the agent workbench. Source: https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom
- Phantom Secrets (`phantom`, this repo): keeps real API-key values out of agent context.
- Locus (`locus`, https://github.com/ashlrai/locus): pins each agent session to one account. This repo ships only an inactive compatibility contract for it (`crates/phantom-locus-contract`).
- Lexicon (`lexicon`, https://lexicon.ashlr.ai): fixes the words dictation gets wrong.
- Ashlr MD (https://md.ashlr.ai): a Markdown app with an MCP server.
- Ashlr Stack (`stack`, https://stack.ashlr.ai): provisions services and stores their keys in Phantom Secrets.
- ashlr-plugin (https://plugin.ashlr.ai/): token-efficiency tools for Claude Code and Codex.

Agents make most changes to this repo through normal pull requests and CI. They follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), use only the value-free commands above, and never need a vault value.
